claim: On KernelBench, selecting the highest-surprisal correct sample gives 80% success versus 50% for most-confident selection; surprisal-guided-top3 matches oracle at 100%.
stance_target: likelihood-confidence can anti-correlate with quality in execution-grounded selection
scope_conditions: GPU kernel generation, not general code correctness
quoted_support: selecting the highest-surprisal (lowest-confidence) correct sample yields 80% success vs. 50% for most-confident selection, a 30% improvement.

breadth.confidence_families: sample surprisal (negative log-likelihood) used as a selection signal; 'confidence' = lowest surprisal (abstract)
breadth.benchmarks: KernelBench L1 (GPU kernel optimization), 20 tasks eval (abstract)
breadth.label_source: deterministic evaluator: correctness and runtime speedup
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present (searched: ECE, calibration); success rate only
